thread.title: Best Buy Is Literally A 'Best' Buy - Best Buy Co. (NYSE:BBY)

author: Yeongwon Kang
title: Best Buy Is Literally A 'Best' Buy - Best Buy Co. (NYSE:BBY)
text:

Overview Best Buy ( BBY ) is likely to have a slow but steady growth into the future. The company's business model provides that stability. Specialization in technology and gadgets is something that people prefer to see and experience in person. BBY's competitive advantage lies in the advantage of brick and mortar stores that online stores cannot provide. It also has the advantage in buying power. Best Buy is a national retailer and warehouse for larger wholesalers (Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ), Apple ( AAPL ), Sony ( SNE ), etc.). Technology adapts and changes over time, and Best Buy will always have new products because it is a retailer.
The largest driver for the company's DuPont analysis is asset turnover. Asset turnover is continuing to steadily increase. Best Buy is able to decrease its assets while maintaining similar sales numbers. This is a sign of decreased waste in operations and increased efficiency. This trend highlights Best Buy's transformative strategy, Renew Blue, and has proven itself by stabilizing sales.
Through the DCF and AEM calculations, we have evaluated a target price for BBY at 97.19. Even at a flat growth rate of 0%, Best Buy is still above its current valuation of $65.59 as of closing Nov. 28.
At an undervaluation of approximately 32.51%, our investing recommendation for Best Buy is a strong buy. In other words, it is the "best" buy.
1.0 Best Buy has a strong business analysis 1.1 Industry Competitive Analysis
1.1.1 Threat of Entry
Best Buy faces a moderate threat of new entrants, although the threat of new entrants in the retail sector is traditionally very high. Best Buy finds relief in the fact that it takes a tremendous amount of effort and time for new entrants to create the required economies of scale to compete with existing players.
Based on its successful establishment of economies of scale, Best Buy has been successful maintaining its place amongst the top of the industry. However, the development of technology and the new business strategies that have followed have allowed e-commerce business, technology service providers, traditional store-based retailers and mobile network carriers to encroach its position by providing products and services directly to customers. In other words, new entrants are trying to enter the industry by developing new business strategies. By taking advantage of a delivery service, such as just-in-time, or through big-data, the largest barriers to entry to compete against traditional brick and mortar retailers - Best Buy - are slowly fading. For example, online-only retailers take advantage of not having offline stores and/or not facing sales taxes in certain U.S. states - both of which diminish costs and allow for lower prices. Brandless, the e-commerce company launched in 2017, is another great example that represents a higher threat to the traditional retailers. The firm manufactures and sells its own products online under its own label. With these facts taken into consideration, the threat of new entrants to Best Buy is deemed moderate.
1.1.2 Power of Suppliers
Supplier power is moderate. According to the most recent annual report, Best Buy sourced most of the products from top five suppliers including Apple, Samsung, Hewlett Packard (NYSE: HPE ), Sony and Lenovo ( OTCPK:LNVGY ), representing about 56% of total merchandise purchased in the fiscal year of 2018. The annual report also mentions that Best Buy generally doesn't have long-term written contracts. We believe the situation gives big bargaining powers to the suppliers of Best Buy. The merchandise acquired from the contracts with these vendors are responsible for a disproportionate amount of Best Buy's sales compared to the total portion of sales which the company is responsible for purchasing from the vendor - lowering the negotiation power of Best Buy. For example, Apple may leverage its brand strength and its ability to sell within its own stores and/or other retail channels whenever disagreements during negotiation with Best Buy arise, fueling the supplier advantage. In other words, Apple has numerous other avenues to sell its goods to; Best Buy accounts for a significantly smaller fraction of Apple's sales than Apple does for Best Buy.
Despite the high concentration and small number of unique suppliers increasing the supplier power, Best Buy is able to harness the power of its own. Not only does the company own a number of brands, such as Insignia, but it also has partnered with specific suppliers like the drone company Parrot. Partnerships with companies such as Parrot make Best Buy the only offline retailer of the product; this exclusivity grants Best Buy additional power over time in that supplier relationship as the company trains its employees to showcase and sell the products.
1.1.3 Power of Customers
Given the technological advancements allowing customers to research and compare both products and prices more easily, customers are gaining significant power over Best Buy and others in the industry. As of the fiscal year of 2018, the trend of online revenue as a percentage of the total industry's revenue is upward sloping. It increased from 11% in 2016 to 15.5% so far in 2018 ( Cranwell ). For example, customers can visit any Best Buy stores and compare the price with other retailers through their smartphone devices in just few seconds in modern days. Moreover, the products Best Buy provides to its customers lean more towards undifferentiated. For this reason, customers are likely to be more price sensitive and have low switching costs.
In order to combat the increasing price sensitivity discussed above, Best Buy has partnered with the niche suppliers - like Parrot, the Paris-based drone company. Additionally, Best Buy has more narrowly defined its customer service specialties with guarantees such as price-matching and the highly touted Total Tech Support membership; both initiatives are aimed at creating higher switching costs between the consumer and the company ( Cheng ).
In addition to maintaining its focus on efficient operations and leveraging the economies of scales to combat this reality, Best Buy's increasing focus on customer service and specialization has buttressed its position near the top of its industry for the time being.
1.1.4 Threat of Substitutes
Threat of substitution is moderate. It is more recently true that Best Buy is facing a growing threat of new competitors, but the firm's threat of substitutes remains moderate. Best Buy's continuous development of its specialization and in-house customer services differentiate it from competitors. Moreover, the company is able to capitalize on more unique consumption patterns in comparison to grocers, for example, to both gain and maintain its competitive advantages. Electronic devices such as TVs and refrigerators are more expensive and generally less routine purchases for customers. Customers not only spend more time making final decisions for purchasing electronic devices, but they also more often than not seek consultation from experts - experts that Best Buy creates through attention and training geared towards employees. According to the study referenced within Ross Cranwell's piece for Stella Services, there is a strong and pervasive consumer preference for buying electronics in-store rather than online. In tandem with glowing reviews for its new Total Tech Support membership, the new Health Technology Solutions service - a service geared toward assisting an aging population with technological aid - illustrates the growing sentiment to adapt and expand ( BBY Investor Relations ). This, along with its focus on specialization, supports the initiatives undertaken by Best Buy and renders the company's threat of substitution as moderate.
1.1.5 Rivalry Among Existing Competitors
Rivalry among existing competitors is high. Due to the abundance of retailers and the more heavy leaning undifferentiated products, this is the case. In turn, this means switching costs are generally lower for customers. Best Buy banks on its brand, services, and physical presence in its competition with local, regional, national and international retailers - not to mention mobile network service providers and carriers.
More recently Best Buy has put the rivalry aside and teamed up with Amazon ( AMZN ) in a mutually beneficial partnership that eases the tension created by other retail rivals; as of the beginning of this year, Best Buy now sells smart TVs running on Amazon's Fire TV Operating System ( Wahba ).
1.2 Conclusion
As the rivalry among existing competition becomes more intense and as the threat of new entrants continues to grow, Best Buy is still in play for industry leadership based on its ability to adapt. Through consistent and successful adaption, Best Buy also maintains a moderately healthy position in terms of its power over supplier and demand. The company's specialization on both electronic devices and services, not to mention its alignment with online giant Amazon, continues to ensure its security. Therefore, it is this showcased successful ability to adapt and shift with the changing landscape of the industry that places Best Buy near the top of an increasingly contentious industry.
2. Best Buy has slow but steady financial ratios 2.1 Profitability Analysis - DuPont Disaggregation
(Source: Yeongwon Kang and co-authors. Extracted from BBY's 10-K Data Reports, BBY Investor Relations )
The results imply relative stability through the past two years; however, BBY's ROE fluctuates year-by-year, indicating that the absence of improving returns for equity investors.
There is no pattern for profit margin, which is not a positive sign for BBY. In fact, this is the primary driver of the company's varying ROE each year. Asset turnover continues to steadily increase. We found out that the increase of asset turnover was driven by decreasing assets, not the increase of sales. Sales of BBY have also been stable, a trend consistent with its transformation strategy - Renew Blue - which was introduced in November 2012 to stabilize comparable sales (BBY Investor Relations). Financial leverage is remaining stable in recent years.
Considering the above facts, the easiest way that the managers can improve ROE is by increasing the financial leverage. BBY's debt-to-equity ratio (32%) is relatively low compared to its competitors, meaning it is reasonable for managers to use more debt to improve their performance. Alternatively, managers may be able to increase ROE by improving the profit margin. To improve the profit margin, managers need to improve efficiency and decrease costs.
2.2 Profitability Analysis - An Alternative Disaggregation
(Source: Yeongwon Kang and co-authors. Extracted from BBY's 10-K Data Reports, BBY Investor Relations )
By performing an alternative disaggregation analysis, it becomes apparent that the operating ROA is the prime driver of the performance - exhibited below.
The variability of operating ROA year-to-year is heavily affecting the trend of the ROE. The spread is positive yet stable in the last two years. Increasing the net financial leverage would allow the management to improve on ROE; once more, as mentioned above in the DuPont analysis, the managers can also improve the ROE by increasing ROA.
2.3 Credit Analysis
(Source: Yeongwon Kang and co-authors. Extracted from BBY's 10-K Data Reports, BBY Investor Relations )
Looking at relevant liquidity, solvency, and coverage ratios, we can see that Best Buy's credit risk is not something that needs to be worried about. For liquidity, the current ratio shows that Best Buy is able to consistently cover its current liabilities with its current assets. Although in 2018, the current ratio dropped to 1.26, it is still in a safe range. In terms of solvency, long-term debt-to-equity ratio shows that BBY stays consistently around that 0.3 range and has been decreasing steadily through 2018. For interest coverage, BBY has shown through its times interest earned that it is stable in its ability to pay off interest. This means that there is little risk of failing to pay interest.
3. Best Buy is an underweighted stock 3.1 Forecasting Condensed Financial Statements
3.1.1 Assumptions
As stated in the business analysis, rivalry among existing competition is becoming more intense and the threat of new entrants continues to grow. Best Buy is still in play for industry leadership based on its ability to consistently and successfully adapt. It is for these reasons that we believe Best Buy will continue to grow, although at a smaller rate than most other companies.
Revenue growth is one of the most important aspects of a forecast. Without revenue growth, a company will eventually fall behind what investors expect on their returns. For Best Buy, the average performance of the past three years justifies future revenue growth. The first year was not used because the company significantly underperformed the market that year. This was an anomaly and thus was not elected to be used in the prediction of future performance. The past three years were more indicative of performance and an average was taken to smooth out the lines.
For effective tax rate, we used fixed 21%, indicating the new tax law, which set the corporate tax rate as flat 21%.
For operating expense/sales, interest expense/PY net debt, net debt/net assets, we decided to use a similar method. The arguments provided above still apply as these are difficult-to-predict metrics. By using an average method of the previous three years, our forecast of Best Buy relies more heavily on the internal trends set in these calculations.
3.1.2 Trend of Financial Ratios
The trend of growth is difficult to predict. Although Best Buy made a notable leap in 2018, growth has been negative for the past 3 out of 4 years. It is because of this a conservative growth rate was used. Best Buy still holds a small competitive advantage in the technology retail industry due to its specialization and buying power. Although small, this advantage will likely push for a small growth trend in the future.
Although operating expense/sales should improve over time due to efficiency, it is not likely to decline significantly. Best Buy has to push smaller margins due to operations as a brick and mortar store. It also carries expensive inventory requiring special care. Due to the business model, we found it unlikely that a significant trend would arise in the future.
The interest expense was also difficult to predict. These can largely either depend on large market movements related to debt items (such as bonds or other long-term debt) or government policies. Because the last three years were similar in numerical value, the average of these was used to forecast future values.
For operating net working capital/ sales, the trend for the past three years was -0.78%. This trend was calculated by taking the average of the 2018 minus the 2017 ratio, and the 2017 minus the 2016 ratio. By averaging this over three years, we can obtain a smoother trend when forecasting for the future. This number is notably high being at 0.78%. Over the course of 10 years, this is equivalent to a reduction in 7.8% of OWC/Sales, an unrealistic expectation even for the most efficient of companies. Although this number might have worked better for a smaller amount of forecasted years, any other number would have just been an arbitrary guess on the performance of Best Buy. By deriving our calculations solely from the historical performance of Best Buy, this is the safest assumption of future financial trends. Furthermore, a complete reduction of OWC/sales is not necessarily the best idea either. Working capital is necessary to perform operations and to grow more capital. If you take all of working capital away, there is quite literally nothing to work with. Smaller reductions in net working capital can be a sign of increased efficiency in operations within a company. Larger reductions can be a sign of incorrect forecasting. A better forecasting assumption would have been to introduce a cyclical trend over the course of 3-4 years. This could highlight the typical performance of a company, where they introduce new ideas and operations and thus become inefficient. Over time, by cutting out waste, they can then lower the ratio again. This would be a better indicator and forecast of the business cycle of a company.
LTA/sales falls under a similar category as net working capital. Long-term assets are necessary to running a company, especially one that is ran across the nation. Without long-term assets, there would hardly be any stability to the company. Ironically, the trend perfectly matched OWC/sales. Again, a cyclical trend might have been better as the number approaches zero. This is unrealistic for a company and undesirable. However, given the numbers, an average value used for a prediction is better than an arbitrary guess.
Last is the ratio for net debt/net assets. This is unlikely to change over the given years, as there is not an outstanding driver in the DuPont analysis. It is more likely that Best Buy is using whichever combination of debt and equity that gives it the lowest weighted average cost of capital. Because it is earning stable returns for its investors, it is not pushing for large growth. For this reason, the average of the past three years was taken again, assuming the ratio of debt to assets is cyclical and stable depending on the ratio that would achieve the lowest WACC.
3.1.3 Sensitivity Analysis
A sensitivity analysis was conducted on Best Buy, which can be seen in Table 5, which measures the flexibility in both growth and cost of equity demanded by investors. An optimistic outlook for Best Buy might include growth increasing to 3% while the cost of equity shrinks to 6%. This would put the new target price of Best Buy at about $124.16. This is nearly double the current price of BBY at $65.59 as of closing Nov. 28.
However, in a pessimistic scenario for Best Buy, where growth is decreasing at a rate of -1% (a sign of going out of business) while the cost of equity climbs to 9%, the stock price could easily fall to $51.61. It should be noted that based on the current price, it is likely that other investors are betting on Best Buy's growth rate to be closer to 0% and possibly in the negative range.
3.2 Estimating Cost of Capital
● Beta is based on the 3-month movement against the S&P index. When a correlation is taken, this led to a beta of roughly 1.04.
● The risk-free rate was obtained from the U.S. Department of the Treasury rate for T-bills ( Treasury.gov ). Since the forecast was done over a 10-year period, the value obtained is the Treasury yield curve rate over a 10-year period as of November 28th, 2018. This rate was 3.06%.
● The market premium was also based on the S&P index. As of November 2018, the implied market return was 7%, and thus when subtracted by the risk-free rate, the risk premium was 3.94%.
● The CAPM model was used to calculate the cost of equity. This value obtained was 7.16%. Our DCF model and AEM model were more affected by the equity holders and thus only the cost of equity was used to evaluate those models.
● Cost of debt was obtained using the 2018 balance sheet values. By dividing the net interest expense by long-term debt, the cost of debt was obtained.
● The weight of equity was obtained by dividing the equity in year 2018 by the sum of equity and long-term debt. The weight of debt was calculated as the difference between 1 and the weight of equity.
● The result was a weighted average cost of capital of 6.48%.
WACC 3.3 Cash Flow Based Valuation
(Source: Yeongwon Kang and co-authors. Extracted from BBY's 10-K Data Reports, BBY Investor Relations )
In order to calculate the terminal value, a long-term growth rate of 1.55% was used with a cost of equity of 7.16%. As stated before, the 1.55% growth rate was calculated by taking an average of the most recent three years' growth rate for revenue, as this was a conservative value that still reflected the company's own growth rate. The cost of equity was calculated using assumptions for beta, the risk-free rate, and the market premium which were also previously discussed. Using these two rates, the terminal value was calculated by growing the projected free cash flow for 2028 and dividing that by the difference between the cost of equity and the growth rate.
As seen in the above, a discounted cash flow valuation using these assumptions results in a value per share of $97.19.

(Source: Yeongwon Kang and co-authors. Extracted from BBY's 10-K Data Reports, BBY Investor Relations )
Once again, the assumptions used to calculate the terminal value used a long-term growth rate of 1.55% and a cost of equity of 7.16% and the justification for these values is the same as in the above section. Using these two rates, the terminal value was also calculated in the same manner as above, just using projected abnormal earnings for 2028 instead of free cash flow.
As seen in Table 7, an abnormal earnings model used the above assumptions and also resulted in a value per share of $97.19.
Also, the sensitivity analysis shown above differentiates cost of equity and the long-term growth rate to illustrate more optimistic and pessimistic scenarios.
3.5 Market Multiples-based Valuation
(Source: Yeongwon Kang and co-authors. Extracted from BBY's 10-K Data Reports, BBY Investor Relations )
The two stocks that are comparable are Costco (NASDAQ: COST ) and Target (NYSE: TGT ). All three companies sit within the retail industry and are major players. Furthermore, all three offer electronics and general merchandise as a part of their product offerings, with Costco and Target having a wider variety than Best Buy.
The ratio used to calculate the share price is price to earnings. Price to earnings is the most consistent and widely used ratio to value companies within an industry. Using this ratio to compare Best Buy to both Costco and Target allows for an accurate valuation of the share price.
As seen in Table 8, using an average multiple of 22.19 and an earnings per share of $3.82, Best Buy's share price is calculated to be $84.77.
